body.p: At some time, long time ago, there lived an orphan. He had nothing. One he [DCh]: Not clear why POSS.3PL at possessee.went off, he was about to wander. He found a small, old tent. In that tent an old woman is living. The old woman said to the orphan: "Go to the west [lit. the place where the sun falls]". The boy went off there, where the old woman had said. Going he saw an eagle sitting on a tree. The boy had arrows. When he wanted to shoot, the eagle said: "Don't shoot. I'll help you in the future". The orphan went on. Going he met a wolf. He pointed his bow at the wolf. The wolf said with human voice: "Don't kill me. I'll help [you] in the future". The orphan went on. Going along the shore of a lake he saw a pike, which had been thrown [out of the water] by a wave. The pike said to the orphan: "Throw me into the water, I am about to choke. I'll help you in the future, if you save [me]". The boy went on. Going he saw a house at the end of the lake. Having reached the house, he entered. In the house an old woman is living. The old woman asked the boy: "Where do you come from?" The boy said: "I don't know where I am going". The old woman said: "Live at my place, I am alone. I can't live alone anyhow". The orphan stayed. The next day the old woman said: "I have cows. You guard them today". The orphan started to shepherd. When the sun was about to set, he lost the cows. He didn't find [out] where they had gone. The sun started to set, he didn't find the trace of the cows. He sat down on a stone, he was grieving: "How can I come home? The old woman will scold [me]". Looking at the lake he saw a wave coming. When it came closer, his cows came out. Behind the cows he saw the head of the pike poking out. He was very happy. He drove [the cows] home. The old woman is waiting for the shepherd. In the morning, when he went out, the boy heard the old woman saying to the cows: "Now you ran away [so far] that he doesn't catch you up". Having eaten the boy started to shepherd the cows. Shepherding he thought: "Why did the old woman tell the cows: "Run away"?" The boys watches very well for that they don't run away. Just when he looked away, his cows ran off. The boy started to run after them. Having a look he stayed back. So he stayed back. He is going all the time through the tundra. It began to get dark. Sitting down on the earth he is grieving: "How can I come home? The old woman will kill me because of her cows". So it dawned. When the sun was rising, at the edge of tundra he saw the cows running back, [and] the wolf chasing [them]. When they were running past, he jumped on the last cow. The boy, crying, frightened them. The old woman opened the cowshed.
